$comment: Operations whose feature scenario is followed by a second identical call expecting 409 (the planner's duplicatePolicy 'conflict' replay, switched on here because the Hub spec carries no x-operation-kind). Each needs the repeat to be a real conflict: the reason says why. sequences: operations run between the target's own setup chain and the target, to leave the target in a state that makes it answer a given status, verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT. An entry answers 409 by default (a conflict, such as restoring under a deleted parent) or, with expectStatus 400, a state precondition (such as permanently deleting a live folder that still has files). A before entry may be { operationId, body } to merge body fields over that step. The first sentence of this comment describes `replay`; `sequences` and `untested` are about 409 unless an entry says otherwise. untested: operations that document a 409 but have no conflict test yet, each with the tracking issue that says why; the Hub invariant requires every documented 409 to be tested or listed here. chainBodies: body fields merged over an operation in the target's own setup chain, by operationId; here createFile makes an element-template file (a fixed template id is safe because none of these tests publishes a version organization-wide, which would reserve the id for later runs). body: fields merged over the target's own body. A before entry may name the target's own operation.

replay.reason: A second review request for the same snapshot returns 409 ('A review request for the same process application version already exists'); verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

The replayed PATCH reuses the revision captured at create time. The first call renames the file so it really changes state and bumps the revision (an update that changes nothing keeps it), which makes the replay stale: 409. Verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: project-deleted
sequences.reason: A deleted file cannot be restored while its project is deleted.

sequences.name: project-deleted
sequences.reason: A deleted folder cannot be restored while its project is deleted.

sequences.name: workspace-deleted
sequences.reason: A deleted project cannot be restored while its workspace is deleted.

sequences.name: not-a-deletion-root
sequences.reason: A folder deleted along with its project is not a deletion root, so it cannot be permanently deleted on its own.

sequences.name: not-a-deletion-root
sequences.reason: A project deleted along with its workspace is not a deletion root, so it cannot be permanently deleted on its own.

sequences.name: folder-has-files
sequences.reason: A live folder that still contains a live file cannot be permanently deleted ("The folder must be empty"); verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: project-has-files
sequences.reason: A live project that still contains a live file cannot be permanently deleted; verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: workspace-not-empty
sequences.reason: A live workspace that still contains a project cannot be permanently deleted ("The workspace must be empty"); verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: template-version-exists
sequences.reason: An element-template file already has a version for its current template version; publishing another one to the organization answers 409 (A version with ID ... and version number 1 already exists). Verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: template-version-exists
sequences.reason: Restoring an element-template version to template version 1 when the file is already at version 1 answers 409. Verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

sequences.name: template-version-missing
sequences.reason: Restoring an element-template version without the required `version` answers 400 ('version' must not be null). Verified live against camunda/hub:SNAPSHOT.

untested.reason: Documented 409 could not be provoked on a live Hub.
The documented conflict needs a migration-created catch-all project, which the public API cannot create.
